Lecture 4: Introduction to Apache Spark
Department of Mathematics, National University of Singapore

Apache Spark is a unified engine for large-scale data
analytics.
▶Unified: Spark supports a wide range of analytics tasks from simple

data loading and SQL queries to machine learning and streaming
computation, with a consistent set of APIs.
▶Data analytics: The scope of Spark is limited to an analytics

engine. Unlike Hadoop, Spark does not provide a storage system.
But Spark runs well on many storage systems including HDFS.
▶Large-scale: Spark is built for large and parallel computations on

clusters of as many as thousands of nodes. The algorithms are
highly scalable and efficient.

Apache spark is a multi-language engine for data engineering. It supports
Python, SQL, Scala, Java and R.
Apache Spark supports a rich set of high-level tools, including

▶Spark SQL for SQL and structured data processing.
▶Pandas API on Spark for pandas workloads.
▶MLlib for machine learning.
▶GraphX for graph processing.
▶Structured streaming for incremental computation and stream

▶Each partition contains a collection of rows of the DataFrame.

▶Add rows: To add rows, one needs to create a new DataFrame and
take the union of two DataFrames.

>>> newRows = [Row(2016, 1, 1, "AA", "1327", "1340", 13),
...
Row(2016, 1, 1, "AA", "1724", "1756", 32)]
>>> newDf = spark.createDataFrame(newRows, arrInfo.schema)
>>> newArrInfo = arrInfo.union(newDf)
>>> spark.createDataFrame(newArrInfo.tail(5), arrInfo.schema).show()
▶Sort: Functions sort and orderBy are responsible for sorting rows.

>>> from pyspark.sql.functions import isnull
>>> newArrInfoNullRemoved = newArrInfo.filter(~isnull("ARRIVAL_DELAY")) \
...
# Remove missing values
>>> newArrInfoNullRemoved.sort("ARRIVAL_DELAY").show(5)
>>> newArrInfoNullRemoved.orderBy(col("ARRIVAL_DELAY").desc()).show(20)
>>> newArrInfoNullRemoved.orderBy("AIRLINE", \
...
col("ARRIVAL_DELAY").desc()).show(20)

An action instructs Spark to compute a result from a series of
transformations.
▶Actions to view data in the console.

▶Logical plan: Logical plans refer to a set of transformations that do

not refer to actual functions to call.
▶Physical plan: Physical plans specify how to logical plan will
execute on the cluster, including which function will be called.
Example: Consider a sum or avg aggregation with groupBy.
▶Physical plan: Hash-based aggregation or Sort-based aggregation?
▶The parsed logical plan is first generated purely according to the

user code. It builds a tree structure without checking anything
related to the actual data, such as whether the columns specified
exist and whether the data types match.
▶The analyzed logical plan resolves the parsed plan by expanding

regular expressions, checking column names, verifying data types,
etc. It requires the Catalog, which is a repository of Spark tables,
DataFrames, and DataSets.
▶The analyzed plan is passed on to a Catalyst optimizer, which

performs possible optimizations such as combining filters and
reordering operations.
▶Spark generates several physical plans according to the optimized

logical plan.
▶The physical plans are sent to a cost model for evaluation. Then the

best plan is picked according to the cost model.
▶The best physical plan is sent to the computing nodes for execution.
▶Warning: The best physical plan may not be the final plan if AQE

▶A Spark job is created when an action is executed1.
▶A job contains several stages, each including some tasks.
▶A wide transformation brings one stage to the next.
▶A task represents a single operation that can be executed on a

partitioned subset of data. Tasks are executed by the worker nodes
in parallel.
1Multiple jobs may be created when AQE is enabled.

CUDA-X is a collection of highly optimized, domain-specific
libraries built on CUDA that includes a suite of open source
libraries for accelerated data science.

Zero-Code Acceleration: Speeds up existing tabular data and
machine learning workflows in pandas, Polars, scikit-learn, and
Apache Spark without code changes.

A key difference between Spark and CUDA-X DataFrames is the
underlying data layout: Spark commonly uses a row-based layout
internally, while CUDA-X uses a column-based layout.

The column-based storage allows thousands of GPU threads to access
adjacent values and apply the same operation to entire vectors, enabling
high throughput.
2Test performed on a laptop with Intel i7-13800H CPU.
